question:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:

When a child is surrounded by a universe of faithful and multifaceted objects, he can just see himself as the possessor. As a consumer, never as a maker, he does not create the universe. He applies it: actions are there, sometimes even in a very boring way, open for him, no adventure, no wonder, no joy. The child controls the whole situation as if he were a little stay-at-home householder; he does not even have to invent the mainsprings of adult causality, they are supplied to him ready-made: he just has to take, he never is allowed to find something out by himself from beginning to end. Even the simplest set of blocks, as long as it is not too subtle, suggests a very different learning of the world: the child who plays with the blocks does not in any way produce meaningful objects; the adult's name does not matter at all; the actions he does are those of a user, but he is a maker of gods. He makes forms that walk, that roll, he creates life, not property; the objects now have their own will; they are no longer a dead and complicated material lying in his hand.

 

What central contrast does the passage draw regarding the child’s relationship with objects?
option_1: One child loves playing outside, while the other is kept inside
option_2: One educated child who is able to read comics and picture books, and one untrained child who is barely able to speak
option_3: One kid gets the attention of the designers by just playing with the toys, while the other one enjoys creating things
option_4: Rich kids with lots of toys and poor kids with limited resources
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'One kid gets the attention of the designers by just playing with the toys, while the other one enjoys creating things'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage states: “When a child is surrounded by a universe of faithful and multifaceted objects, he can just see himself as the possessor.”

• This is reinforced elsewhere: “Even the simplest set of blocks, as long as it is not too subtle, suggests a very different learning of the world: the child who plays with the blocks does not in any way produce meaningful objects; the adult's name does not matter at all; the actions he does are those of a user, but he is a maker of gods.”

• This directly supports ‘One kid gets the attention of the designers by just playing with the toys, while the other one enjoys creating things’ as the answer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Detail and inference questions in Reading Comprehension are answered by locating the exact supporting line in the passage rather than by outside knowledge, even when an option sounds generally true.

 

NOTE

• The other options either reverse the passage's stated relationship, introduce a detail the passage does not mention, or describe a related but distinct idea from what the question actually asks.

question:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:

The Jaipur Literature Festival, often described as the “greatest literary show on Earth,” is an annual celebration of literature, ideas, and culture. It began in 2006 with modest gatherings but has now grown into a global platform where writers, thinkers, historians, politicians, business leaders, and entertainers come together. Thousands of visitors from India and abroad attend the festival every year, eager to listen to renowned authors and to engage in debates on contemporary issues. The festival has provided a stage for Nobel laureates, Booker Prize winners, and debut novelists alike. It has encouraged dialogue on topics as varied as climate change, gender equality, history, art, and technology. Over the years, JLF has expanded to cities across the world, yet Jaipur remains its most iconic venue. The setting of the Diggi Palace, with its vibrant decorations, adds charm and grandeur to the intellectual exchange. In the past, literary festivals were considered exclusive events for scholars, but JLF has democratized literature by making it accessible to all. In the present day, it represents a space where people from diverse backgrounds can share stories and ideas. In the future, the festival may grow even further, incorporating digital platforms to reach audiences who cannot be physically present. Thus, JLF is not merely a festival; it is a cultural phenomenon that continues to inspire readers and writers across generations.

 

Identify the tense: “It began in 2006... but has now grown into a global platform.”
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'Simple Past + Present Perfect'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The question asks about the structure of the specific clause/sentence quoted from the passage.

• Applying the standard grammatical test for this construction: the verb form used matches the simple past tense/aspect construction.

• This matches the definition of ‘Simple Past + Present Perfect’.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Grammar-based questions on a passage are solved by isolating the exact sentence or clause quoted in the question and applying the relevant rule (clause type, voice, or tense) to that specific construction.

 

NOTE

• The remaining options describe grammatical structures that do not match this particular construction — each names a different clause type, voice, or tense than the one actually used here.
